Mr. Thompson has successfully completed the First Shift program. Throughout the program, he demonstrated exceptional commitment and consistency, earning every available point without any deductions.

Early in the program, staff recognized his strong attention to detail and extensive knowledge of industrial and manufacturing tools, equipment, and processes. As Turn90 prepared to launch its new contract with PolyDeck, his skills and work ethic made him an outstanding candidate for the role.

As a result, Mr. Thompson was offered a full-time Production Associate position with Turn90, where he will oversee production activities related to the PolyDeck project.

Tommy is completing his final week of the First Shift program at Turn90 with a positive attitude and strong self-awareness. He shared that his biggest challenge right now is navigating the different ways companies require job applications to be completed, including uploading documents to verify his identity.Regarding his focus area of companionship, Tommy recognized the importance of controlling his emotions and managing his aggression. He reflected on a recent situation at his residence where another individual spoke to him disrespectfully about a door being left open. Instead of reacting aggressively, Tommy chose to remain calm because he realized it was not worth risking the housing support he currently has.He also connected this experience to a past incident while incarcerated, where he reacted emotionally to criticism from a supervisor after feeling overlooked despite his hard work. Looking back, he understands that allowing his emotions to take over only created more setbacks.
Tommy shared that he is learning not to react to everyone who disagrees with him. Instead, he is working on understanding other people’s perspectives, recognizing his own emotions, and maintaining control of his attitude.
He is excited about obtaining his driver’s license before next Wednesday after receiving support and practice from others. His next goals are to secure a good-paying job and reliable transportation. Tommy has remained focused, motivated, and committed to making positive changes.

This week, Tommy recognized that many of the decision-making skills discussed in class are already habits he has been practicing since changing his life. Learning the names and purpose of these skills has given him confidence that he is on the right path and motivated him to continue improving.

Tommy shared that he wants to build a new, positive support system rather than reconnect with old influences. He also acknowledged challenges with technology, such as using smartphones, completing online applications, and obtaining important documents, but is eager to learn.

His current goals are to obtain his driver’s license, find a job close to home, save money for a truck, and eventually move back to Gaffney to be closer to family. Although some family members did not support him when he first came home, Timmy remains focused on proving to himself that he can succeed by meeting his own goals and expectations.

Brought Mr. Thompson in for his first case management session.  We discussed his 90-day goal of obtaining employment that is conducive to his age and health.  He previously expressed interest in renewing his forklift certification, noting that he held one while working in prison.

I reached out to Rachael to discuss the process and expected timeline.  She stated that, based on the current class size, the certification could likely be completed within a week if we are able to find a consistent 45-minute window each day.  I suggested utilizing the Q3 computer lab time, which she agreed would be a good option.

She also mentioned there may be some barriers due to a lapse in the certification grant.  I plan to follow up with Kim, our Director of Operations, tomorrow to discuss what would be required to get Tommy and the other participants forklift certified.

The remainder of the session involved Winard and DiYoung discussing some of the setbacks Tommy has shared during the Q1 CBT block.

Background Summary:

Mr. Thompson (“Tommy”) is a 67-year-old man originally from Gaffney. He was released from Tyger River Correctional Institution on April 20, 2026, after serving approximately 50 years of incarceration. He was sentenced in 1975 on a first-degree murder charge stemming from an offense committed when he was 16 years old.

Mr. Thompson will remain on parole for the rest of his life. He came to us seeking assistance with employment and community reintegration. During his incarceration, he participated in work release programming and spent the last 15 years involved in the PI program.  He was referred to us by New Life off of Broadcast Rd. where three of our other program participants reside.

Mr. Thompson has family support through an aunt who lives in Texas and an older sister who resides in Gaffney.
